title: hermes-gateway.service exits 1 on SIGTERM; Telegram toolset config quirk
claimed_status: LOW/PARTIAL — platform_toolsets.telegram: [] still yields 14 kanban tools (upstream quirk); gateway exits 1 on SIGTERM.
evidence: Root-caused precisely 2026-09-21 in the vendored hermes-agent gateway source (gateway/run.py, gateway/status.py): the gateway deliberately exits non-zero on SIGTERM unless a short-lived 'planned-stop marker' was written first, so systemd's process-exit accounting can distinguish an intentional stop from an unexpected kill. That marker is only ever written by the gateway's own CLI stop paths (hermes_cli/service_manager.py, hermes_cli/gateway.py) -- never by the systemd unit itself, which had no ExecStop= at all. Confirmed via journalctl: every `systemctl stop/restart hermes-gateway.service` showed 'Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE' / 'Failed with result exit-code'. FIXED by adding a new drop-in (/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service.d/95-go-status-f23-execstop.conf) with an ExecStop= that calls gateway.status.write_planned_stop_marker($MAINPID) via the unit's own venv before SIGTERM is sent -- staying entirely inside the systemd unit we own, not touching the vendored gateway source. Verified live with a real `systemctl restart`: journalctl now shows a clean 'Deactivated successfully' / 'Stopped' with no FAILURE line.
root_cause: Gateway's SIGTERM handler does not exit 0 on a clean, intentional shutdown.
proposed_fix: APPLIED and VERIFIED: added ExecStop= drop-in calling write_planned_stop_marker($MAINPID) (passed as its own argv token, not embedded in the -c string -- the first attempt embedded $MAINPID inside the Python source string, which systemd does not substitute there, and crashed with SyntaxError; fixed by passing it as a separate argument read via sys.argv). Confirmed clean restart afterward.

title: SSH password auth enabled (default) on controller
claimed_status: LOW/PARTIAL — SSH password auth enabled (default) on controller.
evidence: Live 2026-09-18: `sudo sshd -T | grep passwordauth` on controller -> `passwordauthentication yes`. Root cause found: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf explicitly sets `PasswordAuthentication yes`, and OpenSSH's `Include` directive uses first-match-wins (not last), so a same-named override placed alphabetically after it (e.g. `99-...`) is silently ignored. Applied a fix (`10-go-status-disable-password-auth.conf`, sorts before `50-cloud-init.conf`) 2026-09-18T14:08 UTC and verified `passwordauthentication no` live. **INCIDENT, 2026-09-20**: the operator reported they could no longer reach the controller from their own PC. Root cause: `hermes` has NO `authorized_keys` file at all (`~/.ssh/authorized_keys` does not exist) -- password was the operator's ONLY authentication method for external SSH access, and this fix removed it. The verification claim in the prior write-up ('this session's own SSH connection remained unaffected') was true but irrelevant and misleading: this session runs as a local process on the controller itself (inside a long-lived tmux session), not over an external SSH connection, so it was never a valid test of the operator's actual access path. REVERTED 2026-09-20: removed `10-go-status-disable-password-auth.conf`, `sshd -t` validated, `systemctl reload ssh` applied. Confirmed restored: `passwordauthentication yes`, and only the original `50-cloud-init.conf` remains in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/` -- exact pre-engagement state.
root_cause: Controller's sshd_config was never hardened like the worker's, but unlike the worker, the operator's ONLY access credential to the controller is a password -- no SSH key was ever provisioned for the `hermes` user. Disabling password auth without first confirming a working alternate credential existed was the actual mistake, not the sshd config mechanics.
proposed_fix: REVERTED. Do not re-attempt this fix until the operator has a working SSH key installed in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the controller AND has confirmed key-based login works from their own PC BEFORE password auth is disabled. This is a prerequisite-ordering fix, not a config fix.

title: Two backlog issues sharing a component in the same campaign crash on a coverage_cells unique-constraint violation
claimed_status: Not previously identified -- discovered live 2026-09-22 while continuing the NEW-16 retry, the first time any campaign in this engagement's history attempted more than one backlog issue (--max-items was always 1 in every prior manual/scripted attempt).
claimed_source: Discovered live 2026-09-22: musematic campaign 7560fd9c-74ec-402c-896c-ab48d2d4e692's backlog-start (--max-items 4, after issue 1 hit a legitimate CURRENT_REVALIDATION_BLOCKED and the loop correctly moved on to issue 2) crashed with sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError / psycopg duplicate key on coverage_cells.uq_coverage_cell.
evidence: Traceback: PostgreSQL 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_coverage_cell"' -- DETAIL: Key (campaign_id, repository_surface, domain, persona, flow, lens, environment)=(7560fd9c-..., source, musematic:general, existing-github-issue, current-state-revalidation, correctness, source) already exists. Root-caused in activities/engineering.py's _materialize_backlog_candidate: uq_coverage_cell (db/models.py's CoverageCell) is keyed on those 7 columns, NOT the row's own primary key (coverage_id, which IS issue-specific -- derived from campaign_id + issue_key). persona ('existing-github-issue'), flow ('current-state-revalidation'), and lens ('correctness') are fixed literals for every backlog issue; environment only has two values. domain was plain `record.component[:120]` -- the only column with enough variability to distinguish issues, but not variable enough when two issues in the same campaign share a component (exactly what happened: both musematic issues 1 and 2 classified into component 'general'). session.get(CoverageCell, coverage_id) correctly found nothing for issue 2 (its own primary key had never been inserted), so the code proceeded to INSERT a new row -- which then collided with issue 1's row on the SEPARATE unique constraint. This bug could only ever manifest once a real campaign attempted more than one issue, which never happened before tonight (every prior retry attempt, scripted or manual, used --max-items 1). FIXED: domain now gets suffixed with the issue reference (f":{issue_key}"), truncated so the issue-specific suffix always survives even if component alone (up to 200 chars) would have exceeded the 120-char column limit -- guarantees a unique domain per issue while keeping the component prefix for readability. Checked db.Finding's own `domain=record.component[:120]` at the same call site -- no unique constraint on Finding beyond its primary key (itself derived from a content fingerprint), so no equivalent bug there; left unchanged. Added test_materialize_backlog_candidate_handles_two_issues_sharing_a_component (tests/test_existing_github_backlog.py): seeds two BacklogIssueRecords in one campaign with the SAME component and confirms both materialize without a constraint violation, with distinct domains -- confirmed it fails with the exact same IntegrityError without the fix, passes with it. 773 tests, ruff/mypy clean. Also confirmed a real, useful side effect of raising --max-items: continue_after_blocked_issue's built-in 'move to the next eligible issue' behavior genuinely works (issue 1's CURRENT_REVALIDATION_BLOCKED correctly did not stop the loop -- it was issue 2's materialization that crashed on this separate bug). Deployed 2026-09-22, commit 207288a, both hosts, verified active with zero restarts.
root_cause: coverage_cells' unique constraint was designed for the audit-campaign coverage-matrix use case, where (domain, persona, flow, lens, environment) genuinely represents a meaningful, campaign-unique coordinate worth tracking once. The backlog-delivery code path reuses the same table/constraint for a different purpose (one cell per GitHub issue) without accounting for the fact that persona/flow/lens/environment are fixed literals there and domain (record.component) can easily repeat across issues in the same area of a codebase -- an assumption that only breaks, and was only ever tested, once a campaign attempts more than one issue.
proposed_fix: DONE: domain suffixed with the issue reference in _materialize_backlog_candidate, with a regression test. Deployed 2026-09-22, commit 207288a.
